beats.vo: Last page, Module 12, Your own bank. run your crypto the way a bank runs its book: a balance sheet, a custody policy, a credit line, a liquidity ladder, a lending desk and records someone else could follow. Keep that page on the desk. This lesson adds one picture: Mastery Starter.

Education only, not financial advice. Crypto and DeFi carry significant risk, including total loss of capital. This is general information. It does not consider your objectives, financial situation, or needs. Past or example results do not indicate future results. Consider independent advice. We do not sell or run a trading bot.
On-Chain Operator. Lesson 12.0, Mastery Starter. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You already keep a journal and a kill rule. A balance sheet is that habit turned into accounts.
It takes about 10 minutes and gets you from zero to ready for this module.
The 60-second version A bank keeps assets safe, lends, borrows and always has cash for what it owes.
With DeFi you can run those four jobs yourself, with written policies, because there's nobody to call when something goes wrong.

A bank keeps assets safe, lends, borrows and always has cash for what it owes.
Liquidity ladder: reserves tiered by how fast you can access them.
Credit line: borrowing against assets under a policy.
Succession: how others recover your assets if you can't.
Fill in the balance sheet worksheet (W6) with rough numbers: equity, L.T.V.
Beginner: Has a balance sheet and a basic custody split.
Practitioner: Runs written custody, credit, ladder and lending policies.
Master: Operates a complete bank with books, tax-ready records, succession and quarterly reviews.
You've mastered this module when a stranger could run your bank from your written policies, with no keys in any document.
